result:
F-DG3-100 is repaired. Every one of the reviewer's 18 forms is now refused by at least one guard, and none is refused by no guard. The finding stays open until a reviewer verifies it, and nothing is committed. One exception to the assignment's file list: I changed the root `package.json` `test` line, which is outside it.

**What the repair adds**
- **Run-time guard (the main fix):** `pnpm test` now runs all the formula engine's tests a second time, as the `unit-formula-nocodegen` vitest project, in Node processes started with `--disallow-code-generation-from-strings`. There, any engine code that builds code from a string throws `EvalError`, however it is spelled.
- **Canary:** a test in that project checks that the flag is active and that `new Function`, `eval` and the AsyncFunction and GeneratorFunction constructors reached through a prototype all throw `EvalError`. When I ran it without the flag it failed (5 of 6 tests), so the guard can't disappear silently.
- **Import allowlist:** engine source files may import only sibling `./*.ts` files, `../value.ts` and `decimal.js`. The engine uses no `@mth/*` import. Everything else is refused, including every `node:*` module.
- **Banned names:** `process`, `global`, `globalThis`, `self`, `window` and the other browser aliases are refused in the engine sources. So is any `constructor` string, template or identifier, except the class constructors the engine already has. The engine sources themselves are unchanged.
- **Scan and records:** the source scan in `fuzz.test.ts` mirrors all of this, with 22 new probe rows. ADR-0024 §6 now says exactly what each guard covers and what it doesn't. I checked the CSP claim against the real header from the built API: `script-src 'self'` with no `'unsafe-eval'`. It only holds where the API serves the web bundle. Item 25 is added to `p3-work-split.md` §9.

**Why the setup is unusual.** Each point below was tested, not assumed:
- vitest 3.2.4 ignores the flag when it's set for one project and only applies it at the top level, where it would also hit every other project. So the new project runs as a second vitest command. That forced the one-line `package.json` change outside my files; please integrate it or reassign it.
- The tool that starts vitest's test processes (tinypool) itself uses `new Function` at start-up, so with the flag on every process crashed before any test ran. A small preload file, `test-support/nocodegen-preload.mjs`, renames one start-up message so that code isn't reached. It turns no code generation back on, as the canary confirms.
- The other routes all failed: worker threads reject the flag, `vmForks` re-enables string code generation, and setting the flag after start-up has no effect.
- Running a formula test file directly without naming the project now makes the canary fail. That is deliberate.

**Per-form results** (the reviewer's probe, run unchanged in a disposable copy; my run-time harness on Node 22 and 24, same results):

| Forms | Refused by |
|---|---|
| O1, O2, O4–O6, N1–N7 (building code from a string) | lint, scan and run-time (`EvalError`; the same code returns 1 or 42 without the flag) |
| O3, N9, N10, N11 (loading `vm`, `inspector` or `repl`) | lint and scan only: the flag doesn't cover these |
| N8 (`self`), N12 (`import.meta.resolve`) | lint and scan; both error in Node with or without the flag, for unrelated reasons |

**Checks**
- `pnpm -r typecheck`, `pnpm -r build`, `pnpm lint`, the prettier check, `npx eslint packages/shared/src/formula/` and the DG2 historical validation all exit 0.
- `pnpm test` passed on Node 24 (locale unset and `C.UTF-8`) and Node 22 (`C.UTF-8`): 1587 tests in the first command (1565 baseline + 22 new probe rows), then 190 in the no-codegen project.
- On Node 22 with the locale unset, the first run exited 1 because one web test failed. It was `apps/web/src/auth/session-identity.test.tsx`, which I didn't touch: a timeout waiting for text, while the other agent was running on the same machine. That stopped the no-codegen command in that run. A full rerun passed, and the file passed 3 times on its own. I'm reporting it as a probable timing flake, not proven.

**Limits.** The run-time guard only catches code paths that a test actually exercises. Indexing an ordinary function with a key built at run time from non-literal parts gets past both static guards. No flag is set in the production API or worker processes. ADR §6 says all of this.

Files are in `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG3/`:
- `T-DG3-KBE-E-kpi-benefits-engineer.md`
- `T-DG3-KBE-E-evidence/` (logs, plus `runtime-layer-probe.mjs`)
